Note::swapcase¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::swapcase() const

Invert The Case Of Every Letter¶

swapcase() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each ASCII letter’s case flipped: lowercase becomes uppercase and vice versa. Non-letters are untouched. It is a niche transform — useful for toggling a display, generating a quick contrast variant, or as a reversible obfuscation step.

The transform is ASCII-only. A non-ASCII letter (é, Α, Д) is passed through unchanged, so swapcase() does not fully invert the case of non-Latin or accented text. It changes case only, is shape-preserving, and returns a fresh Note.

swapcase() is its own inverse for ASCII text: applying it twice returns the original.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"Hello World", "ALL caps", "café MODE"}).swapcase())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["hELLO wORLD", "all CAPS", "CAFé mode"]

Every ASCII letter flips; the é in "café MODE" stays lowercase because it is outside ASCII.

Example 2: Applying It Twice Restores The Original¶

const pluss::Note n =
    pluss::make_note({"MiXeD CaSe"}).swapcase().swapcase();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["MiXeD CaSe"]

Example 3: A Scalar¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout, pluss::make_note("aBcD").swapcase()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"AbCd"

See Also¶

  • Note::upper / Note::lower: move all letters one direction, with full Unicode support.

  • Note::title / Note::capitalize: partial re-casing rather than inversion.
